targeting.title: Ollama llama runner process has terminated: Causes and Fixes
targeting.metaTitle: llama runner process has terminated: Ollama Fix
targeting.metaDescription: Ollama says llama runner or llama-server process has terminated? Read the exit status and the line after it, then fix memory, model, driver or crash causes.
targeting.excerpt: What "llama runner process has terminated" and "llama-server process has terminated" mean in Ollama, traced in the Ollama 0.40.19 source on 28 November 2026: how to read the exit status and the captured error, find the full message in the log, and fix each cause.
targeting.keywords: llama runner process has terminated, llama-server process has terminated, ollama llama runner process has terminated, llama runner process has terminated exit status 2, llama runner process has terminated signal killed, llama runner process has terminated cuda error, llama-server process has terminated signal killed, ollama exit status 0xc0000409, llama server process has terminated exit status 1, timed out waiting for llama runner to start, ollama cudamalloc failed out of memory, ollama 500 internal server error
targeting.summary: Read the words after process has terminated: the exit status or signal says how the program ended, and the error text Ollama captured from its output is the cause to act on|Since Ollama 0.30.0 the program is llama.cpp's llama-server; a memory failure gets one automatic retry with a smaller automatic context, but a context you set yourself is never lowered|0xc0000409 on Windows is a deliberate abort after a failed check or a CUDA error, not an attack, while exit status 2 and the nil ending come only from Ollama 0.24 and older
targeting.author: Ali Rehman

competitors.gaps: States that 0xc0000409 is an illegal instruction exception (that is 0xc000001d; 0xc0000409 is STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN). Says exit status 2 is usually a GPU or VRAM problem and that the codes are stable across versions. Pinned to 0.30.8 from June 2026.

Describes 0xc0000409 as Windows killing the process for a corrupted stack instead of a fail fast from abort. Says exit status 2 has no meaning, without the Go runtime explanation for the old runner. No automatic retry rules, no garbled Windows texts, no nil format, no apps that show only 500.
No explanation of why 0xc0000409 appears with CUDA lines, no exit status 2 history, no retry rules, no timeout, no nil format, no log search steps beyond locations.
Brief; retry description does not give the conditions; no per-ending fixes.
Does not say why the code appears (abort and fail fast), no other Windows codes.
Single ending only; no WSL limit, no kernel log line, no other endings.
Generic; predates the llama-server change in its original form; no endings decoded.
Single cause; not about the runner message.
Memory only; mentions the explicit context case but not the retry tiers.

contentGap: Why 0xc0000409 appears: abort() in a release build ends as a fail fast with that code, and llama.cpp calls abort after GGML_ASSERT and after every CUDA or ROCm error (Microsoft __fastfail and abort documentation, Raymond Chen, llama.cpp b12734 source).
The texts Ollama 0.30 and later attach to Windows codes, produced on Windows 11 with the same FormatMessage call: some are garbled (0xp, hs) because the call passes no insert values.
Exit status 2 on 0.24 and older: the runner was Ollama's own Go program, and Go exits with code 2 after an unrecovered panic or fatal error (Go runtime documentation, reports #12314 and #14291).
The %!w(<nil>) ending of 0.22 and older: a nil exit error formatted with %w when the runner exited with status 0 (Go fmt source, Ollama 0.22.0 source, report #15849).

Exact automatic retry rules since 0.30.0: one retry, automatic context only (above 32768 to 32768, above 4096 to 4096), other models evicted, projector moved to the CPU for vision models; explicit context settings are kept.
Context multiplied by OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL in the llama-server command line, and the 50 percent WSL 2 memory default for Ollama in WSL or Docker Desktop.
How to get the full message when an app such as Open WebUI shows only a 500, and which log lines frame a failed load.
